lesson: The initial holder hides the lower coin rim. Do not fit its straight occlusion boundary as a full circular edge. Segment bright yellow-gold separately from brown wood and fit the visible upper arcs jointly; partial-region centroids are only initialization, not exact cross-view correspondences.
A lifted coin is only partial progress. Success requires the coin inside the bank and both arms home, as judged by the unchanged native evaluator.
The bank's decorative top is not its slot. Bind the actual dark narrow opening in current head and wrist views, validate correspondence and reconstruct its height and long axis before insertion.

A tabletop handoff previously left the thin coin ungraspable. Prefer a complete one-arm path when possible; do not release onto an unverified table buffer or command both hands home while either must retain the coin.

Measure current coin geometry and refresh its attachment after transport. The visible gold region and two calibrated views provide evidence; memorized object poses and old regression coefficients are not inputs.
Maintain separate submission and native-action budgets. Remaining physical actions cannot rescue an exhausted code-submission allowance.
